newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher, but dollar-linked steady.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher, but dollar-linked steady.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday except for dollar-linked bonds, which held steady for the first time after a string of rises, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.17 pct to 108.49
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.19 pct at 108.05
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.17 pct to 109.05
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.03 pct to 110.87
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 107.30
Volume including Makams was 226 million shekels, with turnover in dollar-linked bonds at 20.1 million shekels.

"The market opened with heavy demand for unlinked bonds, causing prices to rise, against the losses they registered in the last two weeks because of the strong dollar. Prices were up on all CPI-linked bonds as well," said Adam Reuter, managing director of Financial Immunities consultancy.
"Dollar-linked bonds were stable, because the dollar weakened today," he added.
Unlinked bonds had been falling, while prices of CPI-linked short bonds had been gaining, as a soaring dollar boosted fears of a rise in inflation.

The shekel surged one percent against the dollar on Tuesday reversing a five percent fall it took in the last week of June in the wake of a reform of the exchange rate regime and a sharp 1.2 percentage point cut in interest rates.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5490 shekels on Tuesday against 3.5870 on Monday.
"Prices of dollar-linked bonds are expected to fall even further tomorrow on the fall of the dollar today," said Ilan Shabat, investment adviser at Israel Discount Bank.
"There is a lot of uncertainty in the market, that is why traders are buying everything," Shabat said.
"No one knows where the dollar is going," said Reuter. "People don't know what to buy, whether unlinked or linked bonds."
Shabat noted that demand for unlinked bonds generally rises at the start of each month when mutual funds customarily buy their unlinked bonds.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.55 shekels)
